blocks.en: # Make it yours
blocks.zh: # 形成自己的工作方式

blocks.en: poteto-mode is one person's style. The machinery underneath, playbooks, routing, model roles, works just as well wearing yours. This page covers generating a personal mode, capturing lessons from a session, fixing the repo so agents stop repeating mistakes, authoring a focused skill, and testing a skill change before you trust it.
blocks.zh: poteto-mode 是一个人的工作风格。底层的执行规程、任务路由和模型角色也能适配你的风格。本页介绍生成个人工作模式、记录一次会话的经验、改进仓库以防 agent 重复犯错、编写职责集中的 skill，以及验证 skill 改动。

blocks.en: Start smaller than you think. You don't need many skills on day one, or even this whole plugin. Prompt plainly, watch where agents fail, and add a skill or a check when the same failure shows up twice.
blocks.zh: 从比你预想更小的范围开始。第一天不需要很多 skill，甚至不需要整个插件。用直白的提示词，观察 agent 在哪里失败，同一种失败出现两次时，再添加 skill 或检查。

blocks.en: ## Generate your own mode with `/automate-me`
blocks.zh: ## 用 `/automate-me` 生成个人模式

blocks.en:
```text
/automate-me
```
blocks.zh:
```text
/automate-me
```

blocks.en: You don't describe your style, because [`/automate-me`](../../skills/automate-me/SKILL.md) reads it out of your history. It mines your recent transcripts in the active workspace for repeated preferences, in how you like replies, delegation, verification, code, prose, and process, then asks you which patterns are really you. It drafts `.cursor/skills/<your-name>-mode/SKILL.md` through Cursor's built-in `create-skill` flow, runs the draft through [`/unslop`](../../skills/unslop/SKILL.md), and opens a PR from a worktree so you review it like any other change.
blocks.zh: 你不必先描述自己的风格，因为 [`/automate-me`](../../skills/automate-me/SKILL.md) 会从历史中提取。它查看当前工作区近期的对话记录，找出你在回复、委派、验证、代码、文字和流程上的重复偏好，再请你确认哪些模式确实代表你。它通过 Cursor 内置的 `create-skill` 流程起草 `.cursor/skills/<your-name>-mode/SKILL.md`，用 [`/unslop`](../../skills/unslop/SKILL.md) 整理草稿，再从 worktree 创建 PR，让你像评审其他改动一样评审它。

blocks.en: Run it again whenever your habits drift:
blocks.zh: 习惯变化后，可以重新运行：

blocks.en:
```text
/automate-me update my mode skill with everything since its last edit
```
blocks.zh:
```text
/automate-me 根据上次编辑之后的所有工作，更新我的 mode skill
```

blocks.en: Update mode mines only the history since the skill last changed. It keeps rules you haven't contradicted, revises the ones with new evidence, and adds sections only for genuinely new patterns.
blocks.zh: 更新模式只分析 skill 上次修改之后的历史。未被新行为推翻的规则会保留；有新证据的规则会修订；只有发现新的模式时才增加章节。

blocks.en: ## Capture a session's lessons with `/reflect`
blocks.zh: ## 用 `/reflect` 总结会话经验

blocks.en: Right after a task that taught you something, run:
blocks.zh: 某个任务带来值得总结的经验后，立即运行：

blocks.en:
```text
/reflect that took way too long. capture what we learned so the next run doesn't repeat it.
```
blocks.zh:
```text
/reflect 这次花的时间太长了。把经验整理下来，避免下次重蹈覆辙。
```

blocks.en: [`/reflect`](../../skills/reflect/SKILL.md) sends the transcript to three parallel reviewers, then a synthesizer sorts the proposals into `Accepted`, `Rejected`, and `Backlog` and waits for your approval before any skill changes. Approve a proposal only if it would change a future decision. One weird session is an anecdote, not a rule.
blocks.zh: [`/reflect`](../../skills/reflect/SKILL.md) 把对话交给三个并行评审者，再由综合者把建议分类为 `Accepted`、`Rejected` 和 `Backlog`。在修改任何 skill 之前，先等待你批准。只有确实能改变未来决策的建议，才值得批准。一次反常会话只是个案，还不足以形成规则。

blocks.en: ## Fix the environment with `/correct`
blocks.zh: ## 用 `/correct` 改善环境

blocks.en: When you correct agents for the same mistake again and again, the fix belongs in the repo, not in your next prompt. Rank the options by how well they hold:
blocks.zh: 如果你不断纠正 agent 的同一种错误，修复应落实到仓库。按约束效果排列选项：

blocks.en:
1. Make the mistake impossible with architecture or a better data structure.
2. Block it with types, or with a lint or CI check whose error names the fix.
3. Catch it with a test.
4. Write it down as a doc or agent rule. Nothing fails when an agent skips a rule, so this comes last.
blocks.zh:
1. 通过架构或更好的数据结构，让错误无法发生。
2. 通过类型，或错误信息明确说明修复方法的 lint、CI 检查，阻止错误。
3. 用测试捕获错误。
4. 写成文档或 agent 规则。agent 跳过规则时不会触发失败，因此这是最后选择。

blocks.en: Human review isn't on the list. A reviewer who must catch the same mistake on every PR is the problem this fixes. [`/correct`](../../skills/correct/SKILL.md) does the work:
blocks.zh: 人工评审不在这份列表里。评审者必须在每个 PR 中发现同一种错误，正是这里要解决的问题。[`/correct`](../../skills/correct/SKILL.md) 会完成这些工作：

blocks.en:
```text
/correct agents keep calling the database client directly instead of going through the repository layer
```
blocks.zh:
```text
/correct agent 不断直接调用数据库客户端，而没有经过 repository 层
```

blocks.en: It reads recent commits, reverts, review comments, and comments that explain workarounds, then groups the mistakes into classes. A class counts once it has happened twice. It fixes the most frequent classes one commit each, at the highest level that works, and proves each new check fails on a real past mistake. It also keeps a table in the agent instruction file that pairs each rule with what enforces it, so a rule that nothing enforces shows up as a repeat. The reply lists each class with its evidence, the level chosen, and why a higher level didn't work.
blocks.zh: 它读取近期提交、回退、评审评论及解释变通做法的注释，将错误归为类别。至少出现两次，才算一个类别。对最频繁的错误类别，分别用一个提交，在有效的最高层级修复，并证明每个新增检查都能让一个真实历史错误失败。它还在 agent 指令文件中维护一张表，将每条规则与实际执行它的机制配对，使没有执行机制的规则暴露为重复问题。回复会列出各类别的证据、所选层级，以及更高层级不可行的原因。

blocks.en: Run it with no argument and it finds the classes from history on its own. `/reflect` and `/correct` split the work. `/reflect` improves skills from one session. `/correct` changes the repo so a mistake class can't come back. Pair it with `/architect` when the fix is a new boundary. [Run many projects in parallel](./07-overnight.md#run-many-projects-in-parallel) has a prompt that does both across a whole repo.
blocks.zh: 不带参数运行，它会自行从历史记录中发现错误类别。`/reflect` 和 `/correct` 各有分工：`/reflect` 根据一次会话改进 skill，`/correct` 修改仓库，防止同类错误再次发生。修复涉及新边界时，结合 `/architect`。[并行运行多个项目](./07-overnight.md#run-many-projects-in-parallel) 中有一条在整个仓库范围内结合两者的提示词。

blocks.en: ## Author a focused skill
blocks.zh: ## 编写职责集中的 skill

blocks.en: When you already know the workflow you want to capture:
blocks.zh: 如果已经知道想固化什么工作流程：

blocks.en:
```text
/poteto-mode write a skill for verifying database migrations in this repo
```
blocks.zh:
```text
/poteto-mode 为这个仓库编写一个验证数据库迁移的 skill
```

blocks.en: Writing a skill matches the [Authoring or modifying a skill playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/authoring-a-skill.md), which routes through Cursor's built-in `create-skill`, validates the frontmatter and links, and ships the result through the Opening a PR playbook. Agent-facing prose has a higher bar than human prose, because an unhelpful sentence becomes an instruction some future agent follows. Let the playbook hold that bar rather than writing a `SKILL.md` freehand.
blocks.zh: 编写 skill 会匹配 [Authoring or modifying a skill 执行规程](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/authoring-a-skill.md)，通过 Cursor 内置的 `create-skill` 生成，校验 frontmatter 和链接，再通过 Opening a PR 执行规程交付。面向 agent 的文字比面向人的文字要求更高，因为一句没有帮助的话，可能成为未来某个 agent 实际执行的指令。让执行规程保证这些要求，不要随手写一份 `SKILL.md`。

blocks.en: One special case has its own generator. A skill that must drive your app and prove behavior is a verification skill, so use [`/create-verification-skill`](../../skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md) and [`/maintain-verification-skill`](../../skills/maintain-verification-skill/SKILL.md) instead. [Verify and ship](./06-verify-and-ship.md#create-a-project-verification-skill) covers both.
blocks.zh: 有一类特殊情况有专用生成器。如果 skill 需要操作应用并证明行为正确，它就是验证 skill，应使用 [`/create-verification-skill`](../../skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md) 和 [`/maintain-verification-skill`](../../skills/maintain-verification-skill/SKILL.md)。[验证并交付](./06-verify-and-ship.md#create-a-project-verification-skill) 介绍了两者。

blocks.en: ## Write docs to a standard with `/technical-writing`
blocks.zh: ## 用 `/technical-writing` 按标准写文档

blocks.en: Skills aren't the only prose you ship. For docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, and commit messages:
blocks.zh: skill 不是唯一需要交付的文字。文档、RFC、README、PR 描述和 commit message 都可以这样处理：

blocks.en:
```text
/technical-writing review the readme changes
```
blocks.zh:
```text
/technical-writing 审查 README 的改动
```

blocks.en: [`/technical-writing`](../../skills/technical-writing/SKILL.md) applies a layered standard with one goal, prose a tired engineer understands on the first read. It picks the document's mode first (tutorial, how-to, reference, or explanation), then works sentence by sentence: who does what, one thought per sentence, nothing readable two ways. Use it to review what you or an agent just wrote, or name it up front when you ask for a doc.
blocks.zh: [`/technical-writing`](../../skills/technical-writing/SKILL.md) 应用分层标准，目标只有一个：让疲惫的工程师第一次读就能理解。它先判断文档类型，是教程、操作指南、参考还是解释，再逐句检查谁做什么、每句是否只承载一个意思，以及是否存在歧义。可以用它审查你或 agent 刚写的内容，也可以在提出写文档的要求时就指定它。

blocks.en: ## Test a skill change blind
blocks.zh: ## 对 skill 改动做盲测

blocks.en: A skill edit affects every future session, so test it like the experiment it is. The same goes for adopting someone else's skill. Check that it makes the agent better on your work before you keep it.
blocks.zh: skill 改动会影响以后的每次会话，因此要将它当作实验来测试。采用他人的 skill 也一样。保留之前，先确认它能让 agent 更好地完成你的工作。

blocks.en:
```text
/poteto-mode run the eval playbook on this skill change. same task for both variants, candidates stay blind.
```
blocks.zh:
```text
/poteto-mode 对这个 skill 改动运行 eval 执行规程。两个版本使用同一个任务，候选保持盲测。
```

blocks.en: When a skill keeps missing and you know what it should do, change and test it in one task:
blocks.zh: skill 反复失误，而你明确知道它该如何做时，在同一任务中修改并测试：

blocks.en:
```text
/poteto-mode update the review skill so it flags missing migrations, and eval the change.
```
blocks.zh:
```text
/poteto-mode 更新评审 skill，使其指出缺失的迁移，并评估这项改动。
```

blocks.en: Asking for the eval up front keeps the edit honest. A fix written from one bad session tends to overfit that session, and over many edits the skill drifts. The eval catches the drift before it ships.
blocks.zh: 提前要求评估，能让改动经得起检验。针对一次糟糕会话写出的修复，往往会过度拟合那次会话；多次修改后，skill 会偏离原本目标。评估能在交付前捕获这种偏移。

blocks.en: The [Eval playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/eval.md) is built around one failure mode, the observer effect. An agent that knows it's being evaluated behaves differently. So candidate agents get an organic-looking task in sanitized directories, never the words "eval" or "candidate", and never each other's existence. One judge scores all outputs under neutral labels, and chain-following gets graded from which files each candidate actually read, not from what it claims.
blocks.zh: [Eval 执行规程](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/eval.md) 针对一个核心风险设计：观察者效应。agent 知道自己正在被评估时，行为会变化。因此候选 agent 在清理过的目录中接到看起来正常的任务，不会看到“eval”或“candidate”，也不知道其他候选的存在。一个评审者在中性标签下评分所有输出；是否遵循调用链，要依据候选实际读取了哪些文件判断，不能只看它自称做过什么。

blocks.en: Read every output yourself before accepting the verdict. If you disagree with the judge, suspect the rubric before you suspect your judgment.
blocks.zh: 接受判断之前，自己阅读每份输出。如果你不同意评审者的判断，先检查评分标准，再怀疑自己的判断。

blocks.en: ## Build a bot UI with `/make-bot-ui`
blocks.zh: ## 用 `/make-bot-ui` 构建机器人 UI

blocks.en: One situational skill is for Grok Bot users. [`/make-bot-ui`](../../skills/make-bot-ui/SKILL.md) builds a small page whose buttons wake a bot over a webhook routine. For example, you could swipe through a review queue and have each swipe ask the bot to act on that item. A server on your machine holds the webhook's sender key, so the key never reaches the browser or the chat. The skill also covers exposing the page on Tailscale.
blocks.zh: 有一项场景专用 skill 面向 Grok Bot 用户。[`/make-bot-ui`](../../skills/make-bot-ui/SKILL.md) 构建一个小页面，通过 webhook 例程让按钮唤醒机器人。例如，你可以滑动浏览评审队列，每次滑动都要求机器人处理该条目。本机服务器保存 webhook 的 sender key，密钥不会进入浏览器或对话。该 skill 也涵盖通过 Tailscale 暴露页面。

blocks.en: **Pitfall:** don't edit a skill mid-task because it's misbehaving. Fix it in its own PR and keep the task moving. A skill edit that ships tangled into feature work is invisible to review and impossible to evaluate.
blocks.zh: **易错点：** 不要因为 skill 表现不对，就在当前任务中顺手修改它。单独开 PR 修复，当前任务继续推进。skill 修改如果混在功能工作里，评审时很难发现，也无法单独评估效果。
